text:
Aisha (Support): Hey team, customer reported their embedding vector length changed after we applied a pinned-model canary for the embeddings endpoint. They say index lookups started failing 20 minutes after the canary.

Eli R: Which customer and which pinned model did they have?

Aisha (Support): AcmeDocs (acct: acme-374). They had a pinned model config pointing at `open-embed-1536:v2` but our canary swapped traffic to `open-embed-1024:canary` for a small pool.

Grace M: Oof, that explains the dim mismatch. Did the canary include a model family change or just a different quantization profile?

Mike (Infra): Canary was a model variant with a different base architecture (1024-dim) — the rollout policy should have only gone to unpinned customers, but looks like pin resolution logic returned fallback to the canary in one edge case. Reproducing now.

Aisha (Support): Customer logs show calls to /v1/embeddings and response arrays of length 1024 instead of 1536, so their indexing pipeline threw `vector_size_mismatch` errors. They also reported a spike in 400-level errors in their app.

Ranjit: Can you paste a sample response from the API?

Aisha (Support): Sure, sanitized curl response:
```json
{
  "model": "open-embed-1024:canary",
  "data": [ { "embedding": [0.001, -0.023, ... /* 1024 floats */ ] } ],
  "usage": {"tokens": 3}
}
```

Eli R: Thanks. Two things to scope: 1) Why did a pinned user get the canary, 2) How to remediate customer (re-embed vs rollback).

Mike (Infra): Root cause: our pin resolution path checks for exact model id in the pin map, but during a config refresh the map was briefly empty for some allocation shards, causing fallback to routing policy which sent traffic to the canary pool. We've got a hotfix branch to make pin resolution atomic.

deploy-bot: starting hotfix-deploy to infra-prod at 2024-08-14T18:22:00Z

Grace M: For remediation, if the customer needs immediate fix: 1) We can force their account to dedicated routing (bypass canaries) or 2) Rollback the canary, or 3) Provide a tiny compatibility shim that pads/truncates vectors client-side (not ideal).

Aisha (Support): Customer asked for the fastest option — rollback canary and guidance to reindex. They have ~250k vectors; reindexing will take a few hours.

Ranjit: We should also offer a temporary API compatibility option: return a response with `meta.vector_length_expected` so clients can detect and error early. But that's more of an API change.

Eli R: For now do rollback + pin lock for AcmeDocs so they never hit canaries during config refresh. Also add a small script to scan indexes and count vector lengths so they can estimate reindex time.

Mike (Infra): Canary rollback triggered. patch to pin-resolution landed and will be rolled to 3 infra shards in 2 mins. I'll follow.

deploy-bot: rollback complete on pool-7 at 2024-08-14T18:26:30Z

Aisha (Support): I informed AcmeDocs: canary rolled back and we locked their routing. They will re-run embeddings; provided script and instructions.

Aisha (Support): Reindex script we shared (bash):
```bash
# sample re-embed loop (rate-limited)
while read -r id text; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDSK" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536:v2","input":"'"$text"'"}' | jq '.data[0].embedding' > /tmp/embeds/$id.json
  sleep 0.1
done < ids.tsv
```

Grace M: Also recommend they run a quick verification before bulk swap: sample 1000 docs and ensure vector length=1536 and similarity scores look sane.

Eli R: Post-mortem action items: 1) Make pin map refresh atomic (Mike), 2) Add canary exclusion rule for pinned accounts (Product/Infra), 3) Add monitoring alert for unexpected embedding length variance per-account (Observability), 4) Docs: explicit guidance about model family changes and re-embed (DevEx).

Mike (Infra): I'll file the infra PR and tag the hotfix with changelist.

Ranjit: For longer-term, consider returning `embedding_shape` in the embeddings response and a deprecation policy for model family swaps that change vector size. Preventing silent vector-size changes is critical.

Aisha (Support): Customer accepted the rollback and will reindex. They asked for ETA on prevention — I quoted 48h for the hotfix and monitoring.

Eli R: Sounds good. I'll draft the knowledge base article with repro steps, detection queries, and the reindex script. Put a link here when ready.

Aisha (Support): KB draft link: https://redwood.internal/kb/embeddings/vector-size-swap-2024-08-14 (draft) :thumbsup:

Grace M: Nice work everyone. Marking this thread resolved unless new errors crop up.

Aisha (Support): Closing — will reopen if AcmeDocs reports any leftover issues.
